description: How SAS missing values behave (numeric . sorts smallest, char missing is empty string) and how to match that in pandas.

missing_value_semantics.title: SAS numeric missing sorts smallest and maps to NaN; SAS char missing is an empty string, not NaN.
rule: SAS numeric missing is `.` and sorts as the **smallest** value; it maps to `NaN` in pandas.
SAS character missing is an empty string `""`, **not** NaN. Keep empty strings as `""` unless the QC baseline shows NaN.
In numeric comparisons SAS treats missing as less than every number. `df.sort_values` puts NaN last by default -- pass `na_position="first"` to match SAS ordering.
Aggregations (MEAN, SUM) in SAS **ignore** missing by default, like pandas `.mean()`/`.sum()` with `skipna=True` (the default).
pitfalls: Sorting with pandas defaults places NaN last, which disagrees with SAS (missing first); pass na_position='first'.
Coercing empty-string char missings to NaN can break exact-match QC against the SAS baseline.

code: df = df.sort_values("x", na_position="first")   # SAS: missing sorts smallest
